headline: A paper reports explanation-free shortcuts in automated interpretability evaluations
summary: An arXiv paper reports that construction cues in several automated-interpretability evaluation pipelines can predict stored scores without reading feature explanations. On rebuilt marks for 500 GPT-2 small features, the authors report a centre-mark rule at 0.979 balanced accuracy versus 0.838 for stored scorers, and a mark-count rule at 0.969. Their separate preregistered ranking test did not show that the tested simulation cue reordered features; an explanation-sensitive scorer exceeded explanation-free baselines on random-offset natural windows. These are bounded author-reported results, not evidence that automated interpretability as a field is invalid.
